newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 11.0/12.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 11.0/12.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 11.0/12.0 percent on Wednesday morning with sufficient rupiah supply in the money market, dealers said.
They said there was enough liquidity in the market despite a neutral money policy on Wednesday morning.
One Japanese bank dealer said longer-term rates were stable but some buying interest of three-month money from state banks was puzzling.
"I don't know why they are looking for it," he said.
Swap rates were inching up after falling sharply on Tuesday morning and dollar liquidity seemed to stabilise as well.
One-week money was quoted at 13.50/13.75 and one-month money was at 14.25/14.50 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Tuesday was 10.47 percent, compared with 10.9 percent on Monday.
